analysis:
The PR changes documentation only, plus one doc comment. In docs/provider/cli-reference.md it bumps the date (line 3) and adds a runtime-constants row at line 2016 saying the watchdog restarts a crashed provider at the next check after the outage is seen (1-2 min), with a 300 s grace only when the restart would continue a crash-loop chain. In ProviderConfig.swift line 23 the autoRestart comment changes from ~5 min to 1-2 min. No executable code, config defaults, authentication, attestation, encryption, billing or coordinator wire behavior changes, so none of the retained threats are altered by the diff itself.

The shorter restart window touches T-043 (watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable binary) and the crash-loop guard. The docs still show crashLoopTripThreshold = 3 and the 300 s grace for crash-loop chains, so the stated control is unchanged. The actual WatchdogDecision.swift / WatchdogPolicy.graceSeconds behavior is not in the supplied evidence. If code changed the grace behavior in a separate PR, that should be reviewed there. The doc claim cannot be verified from this batch.

I also skimmed the rest of the cli-reference text, which is unchanged context: App Attest, add-on hold socket paths, the report command and the prefix-cache environment passthrough. It reveals no new exposure. The paths and token locations it documents match the retained threat model. No findings.
